findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Reconcile the kill switch (needs the Anthropic key) with key retirement: either keep the Anthropic key available to the container (e.g. in SSM but unused) so the kill switch actually works, or specify a different recovery path that survives key retirement, and state which.
evidence: Approach: 'a documented one-line kill switch (`REBAR_LLM_MODEL` back to `anthropic:…`) is the human recovery path'
Scope: 'stop fetching the Anthropic key for this container once the cutover holds'
AC: '`env` output taken from INSIDE the review-bot container ... contains no `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY`'
A Bedrock degradation could occur AFTER key retirement, at which point flipping REBAR_LLM_MODEL to anthropic: authenticates with no key and fails.
findings.finding: The documented recovery path (kill switch flipping REBAR_LLM_MODEL back to `anthropic:…`) depends on the Anthropic key that this same story retires from the container. Scope says fetch-secrets.sh should 'stop fetching the Anthropic key for this container once the cutover holds', and the final AC requires the container's env to contain NO ANTHROPIC_API_KEY. Once that retirement lands, the kill switch flip to the Anthropic path has no credential and becomes a no-op — the very recovery path the ORDERING criterion insists must be proven before it can be needed is disabled by this story's own scope.
findings.location: Approach ('a documented one-line kill switch (`REBAR_LLM_MODEL` back to `anthropic:…`)') vs Scope ('stop fetching the Anthropic key for this container once the cutover holds') and final AC ('contains no `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY`')
findings.suggested_fix: State that the Anthropic key remains fetchable/available for the kill switch even after cutover (retire only the DEFAULT use, not the credential), OR make the kill switch a documented re-provisioning step (restore the key + flip model) and prove that end-to-end path works.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Resolve how the four code-review passes are routed under a Bedrock cutover: specify provider-aware per-pass model ids (opus-family Pass-1; sonnet-family Pass-2/Pass-4), eliminate every bare `claude-*` id on an executed path (they route to Anthropic), and ensure `models_at_or_above` escalation cannot cross back to Anthropic in a keyless Bedrock container — rather than a single REBAR_LLM_MODEL re-point.
evidence: S8 ticket operator-attested comment (measured): 'Baseline (direct Anthropic) = 41 opus (Pass-1) + 1 sonnet (Pass-2/4). The Bedrock run = 0 opus, 19 sonnet. REBAR_LLM_MODEL drives EVERY pass' — 'both single-model cutovers are wrong, in opposite directions.'
S8 ticket comment: 'Bare claude-* names route to ANTHROPIC, not Bedrock ... a SPLIT-BRAIN where the Pass-1 finder keeps calling Anthropic while everything else is on Bedrock.'

S8 ticket comment: "models_at_or_above('bedrock:us.anthropic.claude-sonnet-4-6') returns [('claude-sonnet-4-6','anthropic'), ('claude-opus-4-8','anthropic')] — BARE ids ... On a context-limit error a Bedrock run silently escalates to DIRECT ANTHROPIC: a hard failure in a Bedrock-only container with no key."
S3/2932 Decision C: temperature is FATAL (400) on some Bedrock opus models and rebar Pass-2 verifiers send temperature=0.
findings.finding: The cutover mechanism is a single REBAR_LLM_MODEL knob, but the code-review gate runs four passes (Pass-1 finder, Pass-2 verify, Pass-4 coach) all off cfg.model with no per-pass split. A single Bedrock model id therefore either regresses Pass-1 finder quality (sonnet), or breaks greedy Pass-2 determinism and silently loses caching (opus) — both wrong, in opposite directions. Additionally the Pass-1 model_ladder uses bare `claude-*` ids that route to direct Anthropic, so a bare re-point produces a split-brain (finder on Anthropic, rest on Bedrock), and `models_at_or_above` escalation returns bare Anthropic ids, hard-failing in a no-key Bedrock container.
findings.location: Approach + Scope ('infra/compose/ — the bot service's REBAR_LLM_MODEL / region environment')
scenarios: Cut over by re-pointing REBAR_LLM_MODEL to bedrock:us.anthropic.claude-sonnet-4-6 -> Pass-1 finder silently downgrades opus->sonnet (finder-quality regression no test catches).
Cut over to a Bedrock opus id -> Pass-2 temperature=0 either 400s or is inoperative (resampling), and opus caching is silently zero.
Any bare-id ladder survives -> the finder keeps billing Anthropic while the gate claims a Bedrock cutover.
A context-limit escalation in the no-key Bedrock container -> hard fail (VOTER_ERROR storm), landings stop.
findings.suggested_fix: Make the per-pass model-class configuration a named prerequisite/scope item (the ticket references a config seam / sibling cc33): configure Pass-1 and Pass-2/Pass-4 model ids independently with fully-qualified `bedrock:us.anthropic....` ids, add a test asserting the resolved model per pass under a Bedrock config is the intended class, and assert no bare `claude-*` id survives on any executed path.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Realign S8's alarm to the parent epic's contract: implement the CloudWatch alarm on the review bot's Bedrock InvokeModel client-error rate (>25% over 15 min, 2 consecutive periods) publishing to the existing SNS topic, and record the alarm ARN plus one forced test notification — OR, if VOTER_ERROR is genuinely intended to supersede it, update epic 061c's AC first (staling its attestation) and re-review S8 against the corrected parent.
evidence: Parent 061c AC (verbatim): 'a CloudWatch alarm on the review bot's Bedrock InvokeModel client-error rate — threshold >25% of invocations over a 15-minute window, 2 consecutive periods — publishes to the review bot's existing SNS notification topic. Evidence: the alarm ARN and one forced test notification recorded on S8 (eb6e-f43a-e86b-443a).'

Leaf 061c-scoped alarm: 'a CloudWatch alarm fires on VOTER_ERROR' (Approach) and 'infra/scripts/observability.sh — the VOTER_ERROR alarm' (Scope); the ORDERING AC induces a VOTER_ERROR and observes the alarm firing.

The parent names an InvokeModel-error-rate/SNS/ARN+forced-notification contract; the leaf names none of the threshold (>25%/15-min/2-period), the SNS topic, the alarm ARN, or the forced test notification — instead its evidence is 'the CloudWatch alarm fired'.

No sibling covers the parent's InvokeModel alarm: S9 (8625) records only 'cross-provider fallback' as a rejected ADR alternative, and the epic AC assigns this alarm's evidence to eb6e itself, so this is not scope the parent handed elsewhere.
Divergence kind: contradicts_reality — the leaf steps outside the parent's contract by delivering a different alarm than the one the parent's plan specifies.
findings.finding: The leaf redefines the parent epic's specified CloudWatch alarm. Epic 061c's AC (which names eb6e as its evidence site) requires 'a CloudWatch alarm on the review bot's Bedrock InvokeModel client-error rate — threshold >25% of invocations over a 15-minute window, 2 consecutive periods — publishes to the review bot's existing SNS notification topic. Evidence: the alarm ARN and one forced test notification.' The leaf instead specifies a VOTER_ERROR CloudWatch alarm (rebar's application-level fail-closed signal), proven by inducing a VOTER_ERROR and observing the alarm fire — a different metric subject, with none of the parent's >25%/15-min/2-consecutive-period threshold, no named SNS topic, and different evidence. This is a redefinition of a parent deliverable, not a consistent narrowing.
findings.location: S8 Approach ('a CloudWatch alarm fires on VOTER_ERROR') and Scope ('infra/scripts/observability.sh — the VOTER_ERROR alarm'); AC lines on the VOTER_ERROR alarm; vs epic 061c final AC on the Bedrock InvokeModel client-error-rate alarm
scenarios: Bedrock throttles or returns InvokeModel client errors below the VOTER_ERROR fail-closed threshold (e.g. transient errors absorbed by tenacity retry): the parent's >25% InvokeModel-error-rate alarm would fire; the leaf's VOTER_ERROR alarm may not, so a degrading Bedrock runs unsignalled — the exact silent-degradation risk the epic AC's alarm exists to catch.

A consumer/operator auditing the epic expects an alarm ARN + one forced test SNS notification on eb6e (per the epic AC) and finds instead a VOTER_ERROR-firing observation, so the parent's acceptance evidence is not produced.
findings.suggested_fix: Keep the VOTER_ERROR fail-closed alarm as the last-resort safety net, but ADD the epic-specified Bedrock InvokeModel client-error-rate alarm (>25%/15-min/2-period → existing SNS topic) as the primary Bedrock-degradation signal, and add ACs capturing the alarm ARN and one forced test SNS notification, matching epic 061c. If the intent is truly to replace the InvokeModel alarm with VOTER_ERROR, take that to the epic first: amend 061c's AC, let its plan-review attestation restale/re-sign, then re-review S8.

scenarios: An implementer following the plan literally adds a second CloudWatch alarm on the same rebar/host:voter_errors metric, or re-adds the metric-publish block in observability.sh, producing a duplicate resource / redundant wiring.

AC1's 'commit the alarm FIRST and observe it firing pre-cutover' reads as net-new when the correct action is to VERIFY the existing S4b alarm fires — a distinction that changes what 'committed first' means.
findings.suggested_fix: In Scope, change the observability.sh line to reference the existing S4b alarm (aws_cloudwatch_metric_alarm.voter_errors in infra/terraform/monitoring_s4b.tf) and the existing observability.sh section-4 producer; in AC1, require confirming the EXISTING rebar-gerrit-voter-errors alarm is observed firing on an induced VOTER_ERROR pre-cutover, not creating a new alarm — enumerate any actual delta (e.g. alarm action/SNS wiring) if one is truly missing.
